chunks: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Wahhab narrated to us via an ascending chain, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamran narrated to us from his father, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

My father and I went out one day to the mosque, and he found some of his companions between the tomb and the pulpit. He approached them and greeted them, then said: 'By Allah, I certainly love your scent and your souls, so help us in that with piety and diligence. And know that our Wilayah (guardianship) is not attained except through piety and diligence.'

Whoever among you follows a group, let him act according to their deeds. You are the Shia of Allah, you are the supporters of Allah, you are the foremost forerunners, the last forerunners, those who forerun in this world to our love, and those who forerun in the Hereafter to Paradise.

I have guaranteed Paradise for you with the guarantee of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and the guarantee of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). You are the pure ones, and your women are the pure ones; every believing woman is a Hur' (beautiful-eyed), and every believing man is a Siddiq (veracious).

How many times did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) say to Qanbar: 'Be happy, and give glad tidings, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) died while He was displeased with his Ummah except for the Shia.'

Indeed, everything has a handle, and the handle of the religion is the Shia. Indeed, everything has honor, and the honor of the religion is the Shia. Indeed, everything has a master, and the master of the sessions is the sessions of the Shia. Indeed, everything has an Imam, and the Imam of the earth is the land inhabited by the Shia.

Indeed, everything has a desire, and the desire of this world is the tranquility of our Shia in it. By Allah, were it not for you who are on the earth, the people of your caliphate would not have perfected the pleasures of their wealth, nor would they have any share in the Hereafter.

Every Nasibi ( one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt), no matter how much he worships and strives, is referred to this Verse: 'A laboring, exhausting labor, which enters into a blazing fire.' And the response of a rival's prayer for you is for you. Whoever asks from you to Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, for a need, he gets a hundred. Whoever asks you a question, he gets a hundred. Whoever makes a supplication, he gets a hundred. Whoever does a good deed, its multiplication is uncountable.

And whoever does an evil deed, Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), is his advocate regarding its consequence. By Allah, your fasting one luxuriates in the gardens of Paradise, and the angels pray for his success until he breaks his fast. And your pilgrims and those who perform Umrah are the special ones of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. And indeed, you all are the people of Allah's call and His Wilayah. No fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve. You all are in Paradise, so compete in good deeds.

By Allah, no one is closer to the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, after us on the Day of Resurrection than our Shia. How excellent is Allah's doing towards them. Were it not that you might fail, and your enemy might gloat over you, and people might consider that significant, the angels would greet you with kisses.

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The people of our Wilayah will emerge from their graves on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and delighted eyes, having been granted security. People will be fearful while they are not fearful, and people will be grieved while they are not grieved.'

He said: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated this hadith to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Bassir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) (similarly), except that his hadith was not this long, and there is an addition in this which is not in that, and the meanings are close.

key_terms.الناصب: Al-Nasibi (One who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of the Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Fadail al-Shia establishes the Shia as the 'Urwah al-Wuthqa' (firmest handle) of Islam, linking their spiritual status directly to *war'* (piety) and *ijtihad* (diligence). It emphasizes their eschatological security, noting that the Prophet died pleased with them while remaining displeased with the *Nawasib* (enemies), a distinction supported by the cited Quranic verse regarding the 'Toiling Class'.

en.badr-shahin: Abdullah bin Mohammed bin Abdul-Wahab narrated to us from… Mohammed bin Hamran from his father that Abu Abdullah Ja’far bin Mohammed as-Sadiq (a) related:

One day, my father and I went out to the mosque. We met some people who were taking the place between the tomb and the mimbar. My father approached and greeted them. He then said: I, by Allah, love you as well as your smells and souls. Hence, help us keep on so by means of your piety and diligence. You should know that the loyalty to us cannot be obtained except by means of piety and diligence.

He who follows someone should imitate his deeds. You are the Shia of Allah, you are the supporters of Allah, and you are the foremost forerunners, the last forerunners, the foremost to the love for us in this world, and the foremost to win Paradise on the Last Day.

I have guaranteed Paradise for you, for the guarantee that is granted by Allah, Powerful and Majestic is He, and the Prophet (s). You are the highborn and your women are the highborn. Each believing female will be woman of Paradise, and each believing male will be veracious.
More than once, Amir ul-Mu’minin (a) said to Qanbar, ’Be happy and announce this good news. When the Prophet (s) died, he was discontent with all of the individuals of his umma except the Shia.

Everything has a handle. The handle of the religion is the Shia. Everything has its honor. The honor of the religion is the Shia. Everything has a master. The master of the sessions is the sessions of the Shia. Everything has a leader. The leader of this earth is the land on which the Shia live.

Everything has desire. The desire of this world is our Shia’ living in it. By Allah I swear, had it not been for your existence on this earth, your dissidents would not have enjoyed the pleasures of their fortunes. Nevertheless, they will not have anything in the world to come.

Any Nasibi, no matter how diligently he worships and works, is included in this Verse: "On that day, the faces of some people will be humbly cast down, troubled and tired as a result of their deeds in the past. They will suffer the heat of the blazing fire." (26:2-3) The response of the prayer of your dissidents is yours. Anyone of you who asks one request from Allah will have one hundred requests settled. Anyone of you who asks one question will have one hundred questions answered. Anyone of you who supplicates to Allah once will have the reward of one hundred supplications. Anyone of you who acts one good deed will have it doubled many times.

As for anyone of you who commits an evil act, Mohammed (s) will be his advocate. By Allah I swear, the fasting ones among you will luxuriate in the gardens of Paradise and the angles keep on praying for them to win (Paradise) until they break their fasting. You all are surely the people of the advocacy and the loyalty to Allah. You will not have fear and will not be grieved. You all will be in Paradise; hence, compete with each other in doing good acts.

After us, no one will be nearer to the Divine Throne of Allah than you will on the Day of Resurrection. Allah’s reward to you will be excellently great. Were it not for that you might fail, suffer your enemies’ gloating over you, and people might not accept it for you, the angels would greet you in groups.

Amir ul-Mu’minin (a) said: On the Day of Resurrection, the people of our divine leadership will leave their graves with bight faces and delighted eyes. They will be granted security. While all people will be fearful, they -the Shia- will not be fearful. While all people will be grieved, they will not be grieved.

O Mohammed bin al-Hasan bin al-Waleed (r) reported to me this narration after he had related it to al-Hussein bin al-Hasan bin Eban, al-Hussein bin Saeed, Mohammed bin Abi Umair, Ali bin Abi Hamza, and Abu Bassir respectively. Although the contents are nearly the same, this narration includes some paragraphs, which were not in the other one.
